events.label: Car insurance up about 20% in one year

explanation.summary: How much Americans drive, how much gasoline they burn, and what car insurance costs. The stripes below show every month since 2001: red means higher than a year before, blue means lower. Gasoline burned follows miles driven almost exactly, in the same month. Car insurance follows its own path: it rose slowly for years, then jumped in 2023 and 2024 as repairs and new cars got more expensive.
explanation.methodology: Vehicle miles traveled from the Federal Highway Administration via FRED (TRFVOLUSM227NFWA, not seasonally adjusted, so it rises each summer). Gasoline product supplied (a measure of use) from EIA (MGFUPUS2). Motor vehicle insurance price index from the BLS CPI (CUUR0000SETE).

key_findings.title: April 2020: Empty Highways
key_findings.description: Miles driven fell to 168 billion, against 281 billion in June 2019. Gasoline use fell 40%, to 5.9 million barrels a day.
key_findings.significance: The biggest drop in driving in the record.

key_findings.title: 2021: Driving Comes Back
key_findings.description: Miles driven were back to 279 billion by June 2021. Insurance prices had not yet moved much.
key_findings.significance: Driving recovered within about a year.

key_findings.title: 2023-2024: Insurance Shock
key_findings.description: Car insurance prices rose about 20% in the year to June 2024, and about 50% between mid-2019 and mid-2024. Expensive parts, costly repairs and more severe crashes drove the increase.
key_findings.significance: Insurance raised the cost of owning a car even when gas got cheaper.
